clue.text: Foreign Office initially sends deranged Australian to rummage

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the word sends

parts.note: sick can mean mentally unwell, unhinged

explanation.surface: A diplomat's office dispatches an unhinged Aussie to search through things.
explanation.walkthrough: FOSSICK is Australian and New Zealand slang, so 'Australian' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang, to fossick is to search about or forage, originally for gold in old diggings.

clue.text: Handsome caliph denied last daughter to prophet

parts.note: a handsome sum is a fat one, generous and large

indicators.note: denied last means the word for a caliph loses its final letter

parts.note: a caliph was regarded as imam, the leader of the Muslim community

explanation.surface: A good-looking Muslim ruler refuses his youngest child to a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatima was the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad and wife of Ali.

clue.text: Name occupying chair with English governing body

indicators.note: occupying says the name letter sits inside the word for chair

parts.note: a seat is a chair

explanation.surface: An English name holds the chair of a ruling committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, the upper house in many governments.

clue.text: Dissident, stoical, reviewed Tory cuts

indicators.note: cuts means the Tory abbreviation slices into the scrambled letters
reviewed suggests the letters of stoical are looked at again in a new order

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A calm rebel looks again at Conservative spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges the letters of stoical to IOCLAST. 'cuts' reads like spending cuts, but it signals one piece slicing into another.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast attacks cherished beliefs and institutions, like a rebel or dissenter.

clue.text: One causing buzz, Egyptian spirit loves to embrace unknown

indicators.note: to embrace means the two loves wrap round the unknown letter

parts.note: the ka was the vital spirit or soul in ancient Egyptian belief
love is zero in tennis, and O looks like zero, so two loves give OO
Z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: An Egyptian ghost adores hugging a mystery figure and gets everyone talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A kazoo is a simple instrument that makes a buzzing sound when you hum into it.

clue.text: Grizzly infant to stand with inexperienced reporter

parts.note: to bear something is to stand or tolerate it
a cub is a novice journalist, a cub reporter

explanation.surface: Someone must put up with a green newspaper hack.
explanation.definitionFit: A grizzly is a kind of bear, and its young offspring is a cub.

clue.text: Bar on one Scots town where magistrate held sway?

parts.note: a bail is a bar, as on a cricket wicket or in a stable
I is the Roman numeral for one
Wick is a town in Caithness, in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A pub in a Scottish town where the local magistrate ruled.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiwick is the district a bailie or bailiff had jurisdiction over, and now anyone's area of authority.

clue.text: Sea food from loch within range

indicators.note: within says the loch letter goes inside the range

parts.note: an Aga is a kind of cooking range, a heavy stove
L is the abbreviation for loch, as on maps

explanation.surface: Seafood from a Scottish lake cooked on a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a brand of heavy cast-iron cooking stove common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweed is a marine alga, food that comes from the sea, and many algae are eaten.

clue.text: Lion perhaps devours couple, causing gossip

indicators.note: devours means the big cat swallows the coupling word inside itself

parts.note: a lion is an example of a cat
to hitch is to couple or hook together

explanation.surface: A lion eats a pair, setting tongues wagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is idle chatter or small talk, much like gossip.

clue.text: In passing through on vacation, we're going outside?

indicators.note: outside means the farewell wraps round the letters taken from through

parts.note: bye-bye is what you say when you're leaving

indicators.note: on vacation means the word through is vacated, emptied to its outer letters

explanation.surface: A traveller mentions, while going through somewhere on holiday, that they're stepping out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties a word down to its first and last letters, here the two ends of through.
explanation.definitionFit: By the bye is an idiom meaning incidentally, said as an aside.

clue.text: Brown and green light — this takes two

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
a green light means go, permission to proceed

explanation.surface: Traffic-light colours, and the idea that some activity needs a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the saying 'it takes two to tango'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says it takes two to tango, so the dance is the thing that needs a couple.

clue.text: European in spot gets excited about current spirit

indicators.note: in says the European letter goes inside the word for a spot

parts.note: a zit is a pimple or spot

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters surround the symbol for current
excited suggests the letters of gets are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A continental gets worked up about a pimple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' makes GEST from GETS, and 'about' puts it round I to give GEIST. 'current' looks part of 'current spirit', but it is the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeitgeist is German for 'time spirit': the mood or outlook typical of an era.

clue.text: Mice emptied place for grain left over in city

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside of the word Mice, leaving its two outer letters
over tells us to turn the following pieces back to front

parts.note: a silo is a tower where grain is stored
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Mice have cleared out a grain store, leaving a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the grain store and the left-hand word back to front, giving TROPOLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a large, important city, often a capital.

clue.text: Extent of Crusaders' objective?

definitions.meaning: a unit of land area, an extent of ground
..., a port in the Holy Land, was a key Crusader goal and stronghold

explanation.surface: How far the knights hoped to reach in the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre (now Akko, in Israel) was besieged and held by the Crusaders; the question mark marks the place-name reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a measure of land extent, and Acre the city was a famous Crusader target.

clue.text: Attack SAS, Goering ordered

indicators.note: ordered suggests the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Hermann Goering commanded an assault on the SAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggression is hostile or violent behaviour, an unprovoked attack.

clue.text: Field dismal without young man — top player

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the dismal word goes round the young man

parts.note: dingy means gloomy or drab
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A field looks gloomy with no young man in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense 'outside', so the dismal word wraps the young man.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading lady is the actress playing the chief female role, the top performer in a cast.

clue.text: A race covering one mile demands energy

indicators.note: covering means the race word goes over the one and the mile

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A running race over a mile needs plenty of stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a running event; it means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means liveliness or vigour, the quality of being full of spirit.

clue.text: Military engineer receives credit as fighter

indicators.note: receives means the engineer takes the credit letters into himself

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier who builds and demolishes fortifications
CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: An army engineer gets recognition as a combatant.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapper is someone who likes to scrap, a tough fighter.

clue.text: Northern club actress Helen under stone

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the actress's surname is written below the stone

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight of 14 pounds
Helen Mirren is an English actress

explanation.surface: An actress buried beneath a stone, at a club up north.
explanation.walkthrough: St Mirren is a Scottish football club from Paisley, near Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: St Mirren is a football club in Scotland, hence northern from a British point of view.

clue.text: Smoke and marine pollution here skinned smooth urbanite

parts.note: the Smoke is slang for a big city, especially London
an oil slick pollutes the sea

indicators.note: skinned strips the outer letters off the word here

explanation.surface: Urban smog and an oil spill nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is British slang for London or any big city.
explanation.definitionFit: A city slicker is a polished, worldly town-dweller, often viewed as glib by country people.

clue.text: Married college boy?

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Is the college student wed?
explanation.definitionFit: A married couple are joined together, united in marriage.

clue.text: Celebrity editor held consistent views?

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous editor kept to the same opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'views' looks like opinions; here a view is a look, held steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stared is to have looked fixedly, holding one's gaze for a long time.

clue.text: Help needed to cross river that's dry

indicators.note: to cross here means to span or straddle, so help goes across the river letter

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Assistance is required to get over a river that has gone dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land has little or no rain, so it is parched.

clue.text: Untouchable carcass not to be moved

indicators.note: letters that are to be moved get shifted into a different order

explanation.surface: A dead body must not be disturbed: it is off limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is too sacred or important to be interfered with.

clue.text: One given pound, apparently indebted, angered

indicators.note: given means the one and the pound are handed into the colour word, placed inside it

parts.note: being in debt is being in the red, so red apparently suggests owing
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone handed a pound while seemingly in debt became cross.
explanation.walkthrough: IL goes in RED, so it is literally 'in the red'; 'apparently' admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Riled means annoyed or irritated, made angry.

clue.text: Bounce back as nymph consorting with Zeus

definitions.meaning: an ... is sound bouncing back, and to ... is to reverberate
The nymph who chattered to Hera to cover for Zeus's affairs

explanation.surface: A mythical nymph keeps company with the king of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is for sound to reflect off a surface, and Echo is the talkative nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: Restricted area with monstrous bird in bottle

indicators.note: in says the area and the bird are put inside the bottle

parts.note: a phial is a small glass bottle
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A tiny region with a giant bird squeezed into a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial means narrow in outlook, limited to local concerns like a parish.

clue.text: Season failing to start for Bury

indicators.note: failing to start means the season word loses its opening letter

parts.note: winter is one of the four seasons

explanation.surface: A season that doesn't get going, set beside the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury, capitalised, poses as the English town near Manchester; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it in a grave.

clue.text: Why chicken didn't cross road: exhausted

definitions.meaning: a joke answer: the chicken failed because it was ... by traffic

explanation.surface: A twist on the old joke about why the chicken crossed the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling run-down means being worn out and below par, while a run-down chicken was hit by a car.

clue.text: Debt collector back in action exposed

indicators.note: in says the reversed collector sits inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: back tells us to read the debt collector word in reverse

parts.note: a dun is someone who presses for payment of debts

explanation.surface: A bailiff returns to work and is shown up.
explanation.walkthrough: A dun is an old word for someone who chases debts; 'back' turns it round before it goes into the action word.
explanation.definitionFit: Denuded means stripped bare, laid open with its covering removed.
